dossier.purpose: Self-hosted AI gateway/router (Node.js + TypeScript; Next.js dashboard, an 'omniroute' CLI, Docker and Electron packaging). It serves OpenAI Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic and Gemini compatible endpoints at http://localhost:20128/v1 and forwards to several hundred upstream providers, with per-provider multi-connection pooling, 19 combo routing strategies, cooldown/circuit-breaker fallback, optional prompt-compression engines, local SQLite usage/call logging, and built-in MCP and A2A servers (README.md:8-10, 599, 887-893). For the Codex lane it ships a 'codex' provider (alias cx/) that replays pooled ChatGPT OAuth connections to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, lists GPT-6 Astra/Sol/Luna plus effort-suffixed ids (open-sse/config/providers/registry/codex/index.ts:9-84), Codex CLI helpers (omniroute run|configure|setup-codex|launch-codex), HTTP /v1/responses and a Codex-only Responses-over-WebSocket endpoint (docs/reference/API_REFERENCE.md:640-699). The README makes no GPT-6-specific statement; GPT-6 support is evidenced only by code, tests and CHANGELOG. No Codex-SDK-specific integration was found; SDK or other OpenAI-compatible workers would use the generic HTTP API.

claims.claim: One endpoint for every tool: 'One config — http://localhost:20128/v1 — and every AI IDE or CLI runs on free & low-cost models'; Codex CLI is listed among the compatible CLIs.

'omniroute run codex --model …' launches Codex through OmniRoute with no config files written and credentials injected per process; 'omniroute configure codex' writes the tool's own config; --dry-run previews env/args; honors remote contexts.

19 combo routing strategies (priority, fill-first, round-robin, p2c, least-used, cost-optimized, cache-optimized — pins a reusable prompt prefix to the same account —, lkgp, auto, fusion, pipeline…) plus 4-tier fallback Subscription → API → Cheap → Free.
Account/key pooling: 'Quota-Share routing — split a shared account's quota fairly across pooled keys, work-conserving'; 'team sharing one subscription → key pools with fair-share quotas'.
Compression: 'Every request passes through OmniRoute's compression pipeline transparently'; default stacked combo RTK → Caveman; preset 'Lite ~15% — Always-on safe default'; 12 composable engines.

Compression is decided by precedence: per-request x-omniroute-compression header › routing-combo override › active named profile › adaptive/auto-trigger › panel default › off; the applied plan is echoed in the X-OmniRoute-Compression response header.

Usage observation: 'X-OmniRoute-* cost/usage headers on every endpoint', per-key USD spend quotas, 'live analytics (usage, quota, savings, p95 latency)'; every response carries X-OmniRoute-Decision (strategy/provider/latency).

Local-first/private: gateway and control plane run on your machine, 'no hosted prompt-processing hop', 'telemetry is disabled by default', credentials encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (stated in the privacy diagram alt text).
Radar (signed free-catalog overlay) is opt-in and GET-only; the client does not upload prompts, traffic, provider configuration, usage telemetry or dismiss state.

Agent workloads need far more memory than the image default: the image pins OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=1024; Codex/Claude Code POST /v1/responses needs ~8192 MB heap (container >=10 g); two concurrent long contexts 10240-12288 MB (>=12-16 g); otherwise FATAL ERROR at ~12 GiB.

Interfaces: MCP stdio (omniroute --mcp), MCP HTTP /api/mcp/stream ('110 tools, 33 scopes, enforcement opt-in'), MCP SSE, A2A (/.well-known/agent.json, JSON-RPC 2.0), REST /v1/*, webhooks, remote CLI; a Claude Code MCP add command is shown.

Runtime/stack: Node.js >=22.22.2 <23 || >=24.0.0 <27; TypeScript; Next.js 16; better-sqlite3 with 193 migrations; 'Node.js test runner + Vitest — 39,000+ static test declarations across 5,100+ tracked test files'.
Install/run targets: npm global, Docker (multi-arch AMD64 + ARM64), Electron desktop, macOS menu-bar tray (community project), native arm64, Termux, PWA, from source.
MIT-licensed and self-hostable; 'Sponsorship never affects routing priority'.

code.architecture: One Node process hosts dashboard, API, schedulers and CLI-launched server (docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md:1017). src/app/ is the Next.js 16 App Router (dashboard pages plus src/app/api/** handlers: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses (HTTP + Codex-only WebSocket bridge in src/app/api/internal/codex-responses-ws/), /v1/models, MCP and A2A endpoints). src/sse/ holds request handlers and credential/connection selection (src/sse/services/auth.ts: fill-first default, round-robin, p2c, random, least-used, expiry-first, cost-optimized, strict-random, session affinity, quota gating at lines 1953-2158; model.ts bare-id/provider inference). The open-sse/ workspace is the streaming engine: handlers/chatCore.ts, executors/ (one per provider family; codex.ts, codex-app-server.ts), translator/ (format translation), services/ (combo and autoCombo routing, accountFallback, thinkingBudget.ts, compression/ with 12 engines plus strategySelector.ts/planResolution.ts, codexAccount/ parent+codex/spark child account model), config/providers/registry/<provider>/index.ts (static catalogs; codex/index.ts lists GPT-6) and mcp-server/. Persistence: src/lib/db/ (SQLite via better-sqlite3, bun:sqlite, node:sqlite or sql.js; 193 migrations; tables provider_connections, usage_history, call_logs, key_value settings), src/lib/usage/ (usage and call-log persistence, cost calculation), plus src/lib/{memory,skills,a2a,radar,quota}. Also src/mitm/ (MITM/TPROXY), electron/ (desktop shell), bin/ (CLI), @omniroute/opencode-* (OpenCode plugin packages). Request flow: route handler → handleChat → chatCore (sanitize, optional memory/skills injection, compression only if enabled, translation) → provider executor → upstream; usage written by saveRequestUsage/appendRequestLog.

claim_checks.claim: README says compression is transparent/always-on: 'Every request passes through OmniRoute's compression pipeline transparently' and Lite is the 'Always-on safe default' (README.md:925, 951). Needed fact: is request compression off unless chosen?
claim_checks.evidence: As written the README overstates; code wins and the shipped default is OFF. DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_CONFIG has enabled:false and defaultMode:'off' (open-sse/services/compression/types.ts:421-423); migration seeds enabled=false, defaultMode='off' (src/lib/db/migrations/034_compression_settings.sql:5-6); the master switch is a hard kill that header, combo override, auto-trigger and adaptive planning cannot override (open-sse/services/compression/strategySelector.ts:134, 234-236; docs/reference/API_REFERENCE.md:206); with it off, prompt compression, reactive compaction and output styles are all skipped (open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts:1446-1448, 1692, 2047-2054); the Codex WebSocket bridge also returns the body untouched when disabled (src/app/api/internal/codex-responses-ws/compression.ts:55-56). Even with the switch on, legacy installs stay on defaultMode 'off' until a mode/engine is chosen (open-sse/services/compression/planResolution.ts:141-160). The x-omniroute-compression header works only on the HTTP path (chatCore.ts:1638-1653); the WS bridge passes a null header (compression.ts:77-85). Other body rewrites that are not compression remain on (see risks). No measured gateway latency/throughput benchmark was found in docs; published savings figures are derived or upstream-quoted (see benchmarks).

claim_checks.claim: Codex CLI runs through the gateway: 'omniroute run codex' / 'omniroute configure codex' (README.md:651-662), and README.md:577 says run launches 7 CLIs and configure supports 10 targets.

claim_checks.claim: GPT-6 family is routable through the Codex lane (the README itself makes no GPT-6 claim; only AgentRouter's model list mentions gpt-5.6-sol, README.md:324).
claim_checks.evidence: Code/tests support it: the codex provider lists gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna and -low…-ultra/-max variants (Luna to -max) with 872k context (open-sse/config/providers/registry/codex/index.ts:33-84; tests/unit/codex-gpt6-sol-luna.test.ts:30-62); pricing rows exist (src/shared/constants/pricing/oauth-subscriptions.ts:111-130); CHANGELOG.md:288, 301, 375 record the additions in the 3.8.51 cycle. Caveats: only gpt-6-astra* is in CODEX_NATIVE_UNPREFIXED_MODELS (open-sse/services/model.ts:127-162; tests/unit/codex-gpt6-astra-bare-id.test.ts:57-80); the OpenAI API-key provider's static catalog lists only gpt-6-astra (open-sse/config/providers/registry/openai/index.ts:17-23); the ChatGPT backend gates new models on the caller's Codex client version, which OmniRoute forwards (open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1129-1136). No GPT-6 documentation exists outside CHANGELOG.

claim_checks.claim: SDK and other OpenAI-compatible workers can use the same gateway ('any OpenAI-compatible tool', README.md:639; REST /v1/*, README.md:891). Codex SDK specifically.
claim_checks.evidence: HTTP routes exist and delegate to the same handler (src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:1-60; src/app/api/v1/responses/route.ts:97-139); header-less alias paths exist (README.md:1037-1048). claim_checks.claim: The requested model and reasoning effort reach upstream (docs: Thinking Budget must be 'passthrough' for Codex effort/summary to reach upstream; CODEX-CLI-CONFIGURATION.md:191-197).
claim_checks.evidence: Model: the effort suffix is split off and the base model is sent (open-sse/executors/codex/reasoningSuffix.ts:33-58; codex.ts:1401-1408; tests/unit/codex-gpt6-sol-luna.test.ts:54-62); no seeded alias or family-fallback template touches gpt-6/Codex ids (src/lib/modelAliasSeed.ts:3-9; open-sse/services/modelFamilyFallback.ts:30-101). Effort: default Thinking Budget mode is passthrough (open-sse/services/thinkingBudget.ts:66-70); precedence is forced rule > model suffix > reasoning.effort > reasoning_effort (codex.ts:1428-1433); explicit 'max' is not clamped for Sol/Luna (tests/unit/codex-gpt6-sol-luna.test.ts:64-70). Deviations: 'ultra' is sent as 'max' (codex.ts:1439-1440); effort is clamped to a per-model cap with default 'xhigh' for ids outside the alias sets (codex.ts:319-340); with no client effort, 'medium' is injected in passthrough mode (codex.ts:1416-1418); Thinking Budget 'auto' strips reasoning fields (docs/guides/THINKING_BUDGET.md:20-32).

claim_checks.claim: Account pooling across native accounts with routing strategies and fair-share quotas (README.md:248, 365-470, 576).
claim_checks.evidence: Multi-connection selection per provider with strategies fill-first (default), round-robin (sticky limit default 3), p2c, random, least-used, expiry-first, cost-optimized, strict-random plus session affinity (src/sse/services/auth.ts:1953-2158); Codex connections are modelled as a parent plus codex/spark child quota accounts with persisted cooldowns (open-sse/services/codexAccount/index.ts:40-50; open-sse/config/codexQuotaScopes.ts:9-23; tests/integration/codex-account-pool-restart-http.test.ts); Quota-Share combos exist (docs/architecture/RESILIENCE_GUIDE.md:309-334). Caveat: session affinity TTL defaults to 0, so without opt-in a multi-turn Codex conversation can move between accounts (src/sse/services/sessionAffinityPin.ts:443-453; docs/guides/CODEX-CLI-CONFIGURATION.md:468-493). The WebSocket bridge also selects a Codex OAuth connection (API_REFERENCE.md:651-656).

claim_checks.claim: Usage is observed: X-OmniRoute-* cost/usage headers and live analytics (README.md:248, 582, 589).
claim_checks.evidence: Per-request rows are written to SQLite usage_history (provider, model, connection_id, account, api_key, tokens incl. cache/reasoning, service_tier, latency, status) and call_logs (model and requested_model, tokens, combo, errors) (src/lib/db/core.ts:316-379; src/lib/usage/usageHistory.ts:755-869) from the streaming, non-streaming, failure and Codex-WS paths (open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingUsageStats.ts:37; nonStreamingUsageStats.ts:46; chatCore.ts:716; src/app/api/internal/codex-responses-ws/history.ts:252). Caveat: reasoning_effort_requested/_upstream columns are populated only when the response carried encrypted reasoning (src/lib/usage/callLogs.ts:649-668); call logs are retained 7 days by default (.env.example:1948-1950).

claim_checks.claim: Telemetry is disabled by default and there is no hosted prompt-processing hop; Radar is opt-in and GET-only (README.md:557-559, 836).
claim_checks.evidence: No analytics SDK in dependencies (package.json:302-385); Radar is gated by RADAR_ENABLED (default off) and uses GET (.env.example:3373-3384; src/lib/radar/offersSync.ts:96; intelSync.ts:108); Cloud sync needs CLOUD_URL (.env.example:699-701). But several outbound GET syncs are on by default: Arena ELO from api.wulong.dev (src/lib/arenaEloSync.ts:10, 104, 223), OpenRouter public catalog (src/lib/catalog/openrouterProviderStats.ts:297), npm update check (bin/omniroute.mjs:306-315) and update-banner lookups (src/lib/system/versionCheck.ts:28-36). None of these send prompt data in the code read, but they are network calls beyond the chosen providers.

risks: Provider-authorization/ban exposure on the Codex lane: provider 'codex' replays the ChatGPT OAuth token to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (open-sse/config/providers/registry/codex/index.ts:17-29), sets originator 'codex_cli_rs' and Codex-CLI-style Version/User-Agent headers (open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1129-1151; open-sse/config/codexClient.ts:85-97), and its WebSocket leg uses browser TLS impersonation (browser 'chrome_142', codex.ts:999-1003). The project's own doc says the official session 'is not authorized for proxy/router use' (docs/guides/CODEX-APP-SERVER-PROVIDER.md:13) and ban detection lists Codex among providers with real ban risk (docs/security/BAN_DETECTION.md:114-117). The 'codex-app-server' alternative needs a signed-in Codex CLI sidecar (CODEX-APP-SERVER-PROVIDER.md:14-18).

Open-by-default network posture: the CLI server binds 0.0.0.0 unless OMNIROUTE_SERVER_HOST is set (bin/cli/utils/serverHost.mjs:16-26) and REQUIRE_API_KEY defaults to false (.env.example:400-404), so /v1/* (which spends the pooled accounts' quota) is reachable by any LAN peer; the code only prints a boot-time warning (serverHost.mjs:30-57, GHSA-wmgv-ph3p-rv57). The README Docker command publishes on 127.0.0.1 (README.md:1057-1058) and compose defaults APP_BIND_HOST to 127.0.0.1 (.env.example:128-135).

Model/effort fidelity is conditional: 'ultra' is sent upstream as 'max' (open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1439-1440); effort is clamped to a per-model cap, default 'xhigh' for ids outside the alias sets (codex.ts:319-340; open-sse/executors/codex/reasoningSuffix.ts:11-31); 'medium' is injected when the client sends no effort in passthrough mode (codex.ts:1416-1418); Thinking Budget 'auto' strips all client reasoning fields (docs/guides/THINKING_BUDGET.md:20-32); server-side reasoning-routing rules can force an effort (codex.ts:805-820, 1429); requested vs upstream effort is logged only for encrypted-reasoning responses (src/lib/usage/callLogs.ts:661-668).

GPT-6 bare-id routing is catalog-dependent: only gpt-6-astra* ids are in CODEX_NATIVE_UNPREFIXED_MODELS (open-sse/services/model.ts:127-162); bare gpt-6-sol/gpt-6-luna on /v1/chat/completions follow provider-inference rules (model.ts:592-688); /v1/responses separately prefixes bare ids with codex/ when they resolve to Codex (src/app/api/v1/responses/route.ts:61-95; src/app/api/internal/codex-responses-ws/modelResolution.ts:79-118); the OpenAI API-key provider's static catalog lists only gpt-6-astra (open-sse/config/providers/registry/openai/index.ts:17-23). An explicit provider prefix always wins (model.ts:118-126).

Request bodies are rewritten even with compression off: the Codex transform forces store=false and stream=true, drops max_tokens/max_output_tokens/truncation/background, adds reasoning.summary='auto' plus include reasoning.encrypted_content, injects prompt_cache_key, converts system→developer, removes orphaned tool outputs and, on the translated path, applies a field allowlist (open-sse/executors/codex.ts:250-301, 342-370, 1319-1337, 1364-1382, 1461-1491, 1527-1556); tools are sorted by name whenever more than one is sent (open-sse/handlers/chatCore/memorySkillsInjection.ts:257-262). Memory is off by default in code (src/lib/memory/settings.ts:26-33) though docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md:1021 says 'default on'; input sanitizer defaults to warn-only (ENVIRONMENT.md:276-277).

Fast-moving, very large surface with documentation drift: v3.8.51 (2026-09-29) follows 3.8.50 (2026-08-25) and 3.8.49 (2026-07-28) (CHANGELOG.md:93, 2502, 4096); GPT-6 handling was added and patched repeatedly inside the 3.8.51 cycle (CHANGELOG.md:288, 375, 1566-1567, 1609, 1644); README quotes 358, 357 and 352 providers in different places (README.md:10, 588, 672); README points users to @omniroute/opencode-provider (README.md:642, 756) whose package.json marks it DEPRECATED (@omniroute/opencode-provider/package.json:4); the core handler open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts exceeds 5,800 lines; the dependency set is large (83 prod + 8 optional).

Operational limits for long agent runs: default Docker heap is 1024 MB (Dockerfile:233-234) while the README says one coding agent needs an ~8 GB heap/>=10 GB container and two long concurrent /v1/responses need 10-12 GB heap (README.md:1061-1075); the stream idle watchdog defaults to 10 minutes and synthetic heartbeats do not reset it, so quiet high-effort reasoning turns can be cut unless STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS/FETCH_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS are raised (docs/guides/CODEX-CLI-CONFIGURATION.md:495-525); session affinity is off by default (CODEX-CLI-CONFIGURATION.md:468-493).

Supply-chain and network surface: npm releases carry provenance and an SBOM (.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml:263-289, 442), but no explicit cosign/image-attestation, checksum, GPG or code-signing/notarization step was found for Docker or Electron artifacts (docker-publish.yml:528-582 has SBOM + Trivy only; electron-release.yml:435-457 just uploads assets); build/publish may run on self-hosted runners (npm-publish.yml:66; docker-publish.yml:138); default-on background GETs go to api.wulong.dev, openrouter.ai, registry.npmjs.org and api.github.com (src/lib/arenaEloSync.ts:104, 223; src/lib/catalog/openrouterProviderStats.ts:26-28; src/lib/system/versionCheck.ts:28-36); an auto-update route can run git checkout + npm install (docs/security/ROUTE_GUARD_TIERS.md:62).
